PyTorch documents separate controls for randomness and evaluation. Recommended diagnostic design: save Python/NumPy RNG states and explicit generator states; use `torch.random.fork_rng` for CPU and the active CUDA device, restoring everything in `finally`. Avoid consuming the live training iterator: worker RNG, prefetch queues and sampler progress are not restored by resetting global RNG alone. Use a separate diagnostic loader with its own seeded generator and worker initialization, or fixed cached examples. [RNG documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/random.html), [DataLoader documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html).

Snapshot every submodule’s `training` flag, call `model.eval()`, execute under `torch.inference_mode()`, then restore each saved flag in `finally`, including after exceptions. Restoring only the root mode can overwrite deliberately mixed submodule modes. Evaluation mode controls dropout/batch normalization; inference mode separately disables autograd bookkeeping. Batch original and perturbed histories together where memory permits, keeping candidate items, masks and example order paired. Preserve left padding and read the final nonpadding position. These are implementation recommendations derived from [PyTorch’s module semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html) and [autograd guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/autograd.html).

For comparisons across models, report paired changes in target rank, HR@10, top-10 overlap and candidate-ranking Spearman correlation. These avoid interpreting arbitrary logit magnitudes as comparable effects; softmax probability differences remain temperature-sensitive. Use identical users, candidates and perturbations, define tie handling, and report uncertainty across users. Spearman measures rank association, supporting its use for ranking stability; constant rankings require explicit undefined-value handling. [SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.spearmanr.html).
